title: Brazil banned Bolsonaro from speaking. His AI avatar spoke anyway.
excerpt: Brazil ordered Jair Bolsonaro to stay silent. Last weekend, a giant AI version of him addressed a campaign rally anyway. At the launch of his son Flávio’s presidential bid in São Paulo on Saturday, a video avatar of the jailed former pr
content_html:
Brazil ordered Jair Bolsonaro to stay silent. Last weekend, a giant AI version of him addressed a campaign rally anyway.

At the launch of his son Flávio’s presidential bid in São Paulo on Saturday, a video avatar of the jailed former president loomed over the crowd. The clever part was the confession. “What you see here is not me,” it said. “This is a simulation of my image and my voice using artificial intelligence.”

Then it campaigned. “As everyone here knows, I am imprisoned and silenced by an unjust and arbitrary decision,” the avatar said, before asking the crowd to back Flávio, “blood of my blood.” Bloomberg timed the clip at 46 seconds, and both Reuters and AFP reported the appearance.

Why this is not a normal deepfake

The debate over AI in elections has focused on lies: fake videos that trick voters into believing something false. This clip does the opposite. It announces that it is synthetic. That honesty is the whole gambit.

Bolsonaro is under house arrest, serving 27 years for plotting a coup after he lost the 2022 election to President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. A condition of that arrest is a ban on public communication, on social media or by any other means. He cannot phone, post or speak to a rally.

An avatar can. That is the loophole the courts must now weigh: not whether the video deceived anyone, but whether a disclosed simulation lets a court-silenced man keep campaigning through a screen.

The legal fight

The challenge came fast. On Sunday, a coalition of Lula’s campaign and other left and centre-left parties petitioned the Superior Electoral Court, the TSE. They argued Brazil’s rules bar synthetic content that reproduces a real person to sway voters.

Flávio’s team fired back a day later. The video broke no rule, they said, because it disclosed its use of AI, caused no harm and never mixed fabricated footage with real images. On that reading, it is not a deepfake at all.

Jair Bolsonaro, through his lawyer Paulo Cunha Bueno, denied authorising anything. He “did not authorise the use of his image and voice,” the lawyer wrote, and “could not have done so,” since he is barred from seeing visitors. He added that the former president had never objected to his children using his image.

A court he helped build

The judges are split in tone. The TSE’s president, Justice Kássio Nunes Marques, whom Bolsonaro appointed to the Supreme Court, said using AI to campaign is permissible. What is forbidden, he added, is using it to harm someone.

Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes was sharper. Authorising the video could be a “serious violation” of the house-arrest terms, he warned, and using Bolsonaro’s image to imply he is campaigning could amount to electoral disinformation.

The stakes are steep. The TSE could disqualify Flávio’s run if it finds the clip broke the rules. Bolsonaro himself is unlikely to be punished, said Insper law professor Ivar Hartmann, because he can argue he neither recorded nor approved it. One Lula coordinator predicted the most heavily litigated election since Brazil returned to democracy.

The rules are already behind

Politicians are reaching for avatars faster than the law can frame them. Malaysia’s prime minister has fielded his own AI stand-in, and regulators are scrambling to respond. France plans to triple the penalties for AI-driven election disinformation.

Most of those rules turn on disclosure. The EU’s AI Act will force a label on synthetic media, and Brazil’s own code targets fabricated content that misleads. The Bolsonaro clip met that bar and marched straight through it. India is wrestling with the flip side, opening a case over altered videos of its prime minister.

That is the gap this stunt exposes. A label tells you a video is fake. It does not tell you whether a jailed politician should be allowed to speak through it. Brazil votes on 4 October. Its court has until then to decide.

content_html_zh:
巴西要求雅伊尔·博尔索纳罗保持沉默。 上周末，他的一个巨大的人工智能版本在一次竞选集会上发表了讲话。

周六，在他的儿子弗拉维奥在圣保罗竞选总统时，这位被监禁的前总统的视频头像出现在人群中。 最聪明的部分是坦白。 “你在这里看到的不是我，”它说。 “这是使用人工智能对我的图像和声音进行的模拟。”

然后它开展了竞选活动。 “这里的每个人都知道，我因一个不公正和武断的决定而被监禁和沉默，”化身说道，然后要求人群支持弗拉维奥，“我的血。” 彭博社将这段视频定为 46 秒，路透社和法新社都报道了这一事件。

为什么这不是普通的深度伪造

关于人工智能在选举中的争论主要集中在谎言上：虚假视频欺骗选民相信一些错误的东西。 这个剪辑的作用恰恰相反。 它宣布它是合成的。 诚实就是整个策略。

博尔索纳罗在 2022 年选举中输给总统路易斯·伊纳西奥·卢拉·达席尔瓦后，因策划政变而被软禁 27 年。 逮捕的一个条件是禁止通过社交媒体或任何其他方式进行公共交流。 他无法打电话、发帖或在集会上发言。

头像可以。 这是法院现在必须权衡的漏洞：不是视频是否欺骗了任何人，而是披露的模拟是否让法庭沉默的人继续通过屏幕进行竞选活动。

法律斗争

挑战来得很快。 周日，卢拉竞选团队和其他左翼和中左翼政党联盟向高级选举法院（TSE）请愿。 他们认为，巴西的规定禁止复制真人的合成内容来影响选民。

一天后，弗拉维奥的团队进行了还击。 他们说，该视频没有违反规则，因为它披露了人工智能的使用，没有造成任何伤害，而且从未将捏造的镜头与真实图像混合在一起。 读起来，它根本不是深度伪造的。

雅伊尔·博尔索纳罗通过他的律师保罗·库尼亚·布埃诺否认授权任何事情。 律师写道，他“没有授权使用他的形象和声音”，而且“也不可能这样做”，因为他被禁止会见访客。 他补充说，前总统从未反对他的孩子使用他的形象。

他帮助建造的法院

评委们语气不一。 被博尔索纳罗任命为最高法院法官的 TSE 主席卡西奥·努内斯·马克斯 (Kássio Nunes Marques) 法官表示，使用人工智能进行竞选是允许的。 他补充说，禁止的是使用它来伤害某人。

最高法院法官亚历山大·德·莫赖斯（Alexandre de Moraes）的态度更为犀利。 他警告说，授权播放这段视频可能“严重违反”软禁条款，而利用博尔索纳罗的形象暗示他正在竞选可能构成选举虚假信息。

赌注很大。 如果 TSE 发现该片段违反规则，可能会取消弗拉维奥的竞选资格。 因斯珀法学教授伊瓦尔·哈特曼表示，博尔索纳罗本人不太可能受到惩罚，因为他可以辩称自己既没有记录也没有批准这件事。 一名卢拉协调员预测，这将是巴西恢复民主以来诉讼最严重的选举。

规则已经落后了

政客们寻找化身的速度比法律规定他们的速度还要快。 马来西亚总理派出了自己的人工智能替身，监管机构正忙于回应。 法国计划将对人工智能驱动的选举虚假信息的处罚增加三倍。

这些规则大部分都以信息披露为基础。 欧盟的《人工智能法案》将强制在合成媒体上贴上标签，而巴西自己的法规则针对捏造的误导性内容。 博尔索纳罗的视频遇到了那个酒吧，然后径直穿过了它。 印度正在努力应对另一面，就其总理视频被篡改提起诉讼。

这就是这个特技暴露的差距。 标签告诉您视频是假的。 它并没有告诉你是否应该允许被监禁的政客通过它发表讲话。 巴西将于 10 月 4 日投票。 法院必须在此之前做出决定。
